title: init generates provider config and workflows on a bare repository
expectation: On a repository with no manifests, `monochange init --provider github` writes `monochange.toml` plus `.github/workflows/changeset-policy.yml` and `.github/workflows/release.yml`, activates a `[source]` table with `provider = "github"`, and ships no `[cli.*]` tables; the generated config passes `monochange step validate` even with zero packages. Plain `init` writes a provider-neutral config with no active `[source]` table. A second `init` refuses without `--force` and succeeds with it. Workflows are github-only: `--provider gitlab` writes config without `.github/`. `init` accepts only `github|gitlab|gitea` — `forgejo`, which `[source]` config itself accepts, is rejected with exit 1 and writes nothing. Every check removes what it generates so later checks start from the bare fixture.
setupCommands: git init -q && git add -A && git commit -S -qm 'initial commit'

checks.command: monochange init --provider github && test -f monochange.toml && test -f .github/workflows/changeset-policy.yml && test -f .github/workflows/release.yml; rc=$?; rm -f monochange.toml; rm -rf .github; exit $rc
checks.why: The github provider must scaffold the release automation CI together with the config; a workflow that stops being written is a silent regression no later step catches.

checks.command: monochange init --provider github >/dev/null 2>&1 && grep -q '^provider = "github"' monochange.toml && ! grep -q '^\[cli\.' monochange.toml; rc=$?; rm -f monochange.toml; rm -rf .github; exit $rc
checks.why: The generated `[source]` table must be active (not commented out), and the documented starter shape is minimal: no `[cli.*]` command aliases.

checks.command: monochange init --provider github >/dev/null 2>&1 && monochange step validate; rc=$?; rm -f monochange.toml; rm -rf .github; exit $rc
checks.why: The first config a new user receives must parse and validate even before any package exists.

checks.command: monochange init >/dev/null 2>&1 && test -f monochange.toml && ! grep -q '^\[source\]' monochange.toml; rc=$?; rm -f monochange.toml; rm -rf .github; exit $rc
checks.why: Without `--provider` the starter config is provider-neutral: no active `[source]` table, so no release automation silently targets github.

checks.command: monochange init >/dev/null 2>&1 && monochange init --provider github; rc=$?; rm -f monochange.toml; rm -rf .github; test $rc -ne 0
checks.why: A starter-config generator must never clobber an existing `monochange.toml` without the explicit override, and must say which flag supplies it.

checks.command: monochange init >/dev/null 2>&1 && monochange init --provider github --force; rc=$?; rm -f monochange.toml; rm -rf .github; exit $rc
checks.why: The explicit override must exist and regenerate the full scaffold over an existing config.

checks.command: monochange init --provider gitlab >/dev/null 2>&1 && grep -q '^provider = "gitlab"' monochange.toml && test ! -e .github; rc=$?; rm -f monochange.toml; rm -rf .github; exit $rc
checks.why: Actions workflows are github-only: gitlab (and gitea) get provider config and settings without a `.github/` tree that could never run.

checks.command: monochange init --provider forgejo; rc=$?; rm -f monochange.toml; rm -rf .github; test $rc -ne 0
checks.why: `[source]` config accepts forgejo but `init` does not; pinning the real boundary means any widening or narrowing of the provider set is a deliberate change.
